# COR020 `initialisation-in-declaration`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A procedure's local variable is initialised in its declaration, which implies `save`.

## Why

In Fortran an initialiser in a declaration is not executed at each call: it gives the variable the
SAVE attribute and sets it once, before the program starts. `integer :: count = 0` keeps the value
of the previous call, and in multi-threaded code (OpenMP, OpenACC) the single static copy is shared
by every thread, a data race. Assign the initial value in an executable statement, or write `save`
explicitly when persistence is intended.

## Reported

```fortran
subroutine accumulate(x)
  real, intent(in) :: x
  real :: total = 0.0   ! set once, then keeps growing across calls
```

## Preferred

```fortran
subroutine accumulate(x)
  real, intent(in) :: x
  real :: total
  total = 0.0
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR020] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR020` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C081` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
